title: Scoring RNA Structure Prediction on Interventions That Have Already Been Performed
one_line: An instrument paper. It recovers controlled two-nucleotide interventions already executed in a public chemical-probing corpus, scores three structure predictors by their response rather than by agreement with a reference, and prices eight channels through which a benchmark number can be carried by a covariate somebody chose.
abstract_as_printed: Chemical-probing benchmarks score RNA structure predictors by how far a predicted structure agrees with a reference. We argue, and measure, that such a number is not self-interpreting, and that it fails in two separate ways. It can be carried by a covariate somebody chose -- these corpora are written by design programs, filtered by a rule, mutated at pairs an experimenter picked, and scored against a column that is itself a model's output. And it can be entirely real and still buy nothing, because agreement is not the quantity an experimenter acts on. We build an instrument that makes both readable on the same molecules. Compensatory orientation flips already executed in a public corpus are recovered by a stated criterion -- 4317 two-nucleotide interventions whose outcome is measured and contains no folding model -- and 4 independent predictor implementations are scored by their response to them rather than by their agreement with a reference. The corpus supplies its own null: constructs whose designed substitution is null were synthesised and probed anyway, and 23.0% of them cross the threshold at which this paper calls an intervention rescued. That is a measured false-positive rate for the outcome, and we are aware of no benchmark in this neighbourhood that reports one. Read this way, the incumbent benchmark's margin does not survive translation into an experiment. At a fixed budget no implementation outperforms helix depth -- an integer read off the declared target structure, free wherever a target is declared -- and 9 of 12 comparisons are formally equivalent to it within the gain one extra construct buys; the panel's largest agreement margin, +0.260, is worth 1.0% of this corpus's rescuing interventions; and the gap changes sign exactly 1 time as budget is swept, at 15.0%--17.5% of a design built. A model's agreement advantage is an average, and the better it ranks on that average the further from the top of its own ranked list the advantage lies -- while a budgeted experimenter only ever sees the top. The same molecules also price 8 covariate-choice channels -- 5 carry the number, 1 bounded and empty, 2 unresolved. Every agreement number here is labelled by the reference it is scored against, because the structure column this benchmark ships is a model's own output: the interventional reading separates from the agreement reading by +0.2367SD ([+0.1151, +0.3755]) even when the agreement column is a reference reconstructed from this deposit's own probing data rather than predicted from sequence by any scored model, and against that reconstructed reference the incumbent's largest margin loses 41% of its size. Prices are reported as direct contrasts and never as shares, because the estimator for a share is uninformative here, which we show and withdraw a metric of our own for. This instrument's domain cannot be found; it has to be built, and we specify it. The largest public probing corpus, 806{,}573 sequences over 23 libraries, holds 205 candidate orientation-flip sequence pairs in total, because diversity and intervention are in direct tension: a design library spends every slot on a new molecule and an intervention needs four spent on one. The specification that follows is four measured lines -- $4n$ slots per $n$ interventions, reference signal-to-noise above 9.33, per-construct design windows and declared targets, and enough probing to check those targets, since a probing-derived reference confirms only 77% of the pairs these design programs declared.
canonical_estimand_as_printed: Because the rest of the paper depends on it, the estimand is written here rather than assembled from context. This instrument does not measure whether a predicted structure is globally correct. It measures whether a predictor's probability for a named base pair anticipates the measured consequence of a specific compensatory intervention on that pair, in a molecule whose own wild type is the internal control. Everything that follows is an application of that one quantity: Reading 1 asks who chose the covariates it varies over, Reading 2 asks what a margin in it is worth as an experiment, and the domain analysis asks which corpora can supply it at all. A benchmark scored on global agreement answers a different question, and this paper does not claim that question is the wrong one -- only that its answer does not transfer to this one by default.

The corpus was not sampled: design programs wrote the molecules, a rule chose which were made, experimenters chose which pairs to mutate, and the reference against which agreement is scored is itself a model's output. In that setting a benchmark number is carried by a covariate somebody chose, and an instrument's work is to name each chooser and price the channel. claim_quotes_as_printed.verbatim_as_printed: Across 4 independent implementations and three budgets -- and a fifth, the only pseudoknot-capable one, added because this corpus is a pseudoknot round and losing at every budget (+0.1321 against +0.1613 at the tightest) -- no model outperforms a free integer as a standalone ranker of which interventions to build: none of 12 intervals excludes zero, and against a margin fixed as the gain one extra construct buys ($delta=+0.0473$), 9 are equivalent to free depth while the remaining 3 fail on the side of being worse. The panel's largest structure-agreement margin, +0.260, converts to 1.0% of this corpus's rescuing interventions, and at the tightest budget its sign inverts (-0.0159 [-0.0278, -0.0036]) -- a measured crossing rather than three points: swept over 19 budgets the gap changes sign exactly 1 time, at 15.0%--17.5% of a design built, surviving any dropped target, 4 of 5 rescue thresholds, and 5 of 6 predictor pairs -- the only pair that does not invert being two implementations of one model family. A structure-benchmark margin is an average, and the better a model ranks on that average the further from the top of its own list its advantage lies. A budgeted experimenter only ever sees the top.

Thermodynamic models minimise or sum a free energy over a nearest-neighbour decomposition of the structure zuker1981optimal,mccaskill1990equilibrium, hofacker1994fast,lorenz2011vienna, with parameters measured by optical melting on short duplexes, coaxial stacks and helix ends freier1986improved,walter1994coaxial,serra1995predicting, xia1998thermodynamic,mathews1999expanded,turner2010nndb. Neural models drop the decomposition and predict pairing from sequence with a learned architecture and no explicit energy singh2019spotrna,sato2021rna,fu2022ufold, ribonanzanet2024.
